text.p: Horsham Corp said on Tuesday it proposed a merger with 48 percent-owned real estate firm Trizec Corp Ltd in a long-awaited move to stimulate Horsham's stock price.

The merged entity would be called Trizec Hahn Corp. Under the proposed deal, Trizec shareholders other than Horsham would receive 0.58 of a subordinated voting share of Trizec Hahn for each Trizec common share.
Subject to the approval of Trizec Hahn's board, Horsham also proposed that the merged entity raise dividends with an initial increase to US$0.25 a share.
Peter Munk would be chairman and chief executive of Trizec Hahn, while Greg Wilkins, now president of Horsham and Trizec, would become president and chief operating officer of the merged entity.

Trizec established a special committee of the board of directors to consider the Horsham proposal, Horsham said. The deal is subject to the approval of appropriate regulatory authorities as well as the holders of a majority of Trizec's common shares other than Horsham.
The proposal was based on arm's length talks with Argo Partnership L.P., Trizec's 26 percent shareholder.
